package_info.why_malicious: The package embeds unauthorized cryptomining scripts in the HTML it serves, causing visitors' browsers to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker's benefit without user knowledge or consent. This activity is not disclosed in the package documentation and is unrelated to the intended function of providing a maintenance mode website. The malicious code remained in the npm package even after being removed from the public source repository, indicating a supply chain integrity compromise.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits a page served by the package
execution_context.file_location: index.html (embedded in the HTML served by the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user visits a page served by the package, the code loads a remote cryptomining script from coinhive.com, instantiates a CoinHive.Anonymous miner with the attacker's site key, uses up to half of the user's available CPU threads with no throttling, and sends mined cryptocurrency shares to the attacker's account.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code loads a third-party cryptomining script from coinhive.com and initiates mining in the user's browser without any notification or consent, directly exploiting visitor resources for the attacker's gain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A maintenance mode website should only display a static or informational page and should not execute background scripts, especially those that consume significant CPU or contact cryptomining domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate cryptomining scripts may be used on opt-in mining sites or as an alternative to ads, but only with explicit user consent and clear disclosure to users.
key_indicators: Instantiation of CoinHive.Anonymous with a hardcoded site key
No user notification or consent mechanism present
High browser CPU usage upon page load

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits a page served by the package (earlier commit variant)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user visits a page served by the package, the code loads a cryptomining script from coin-hive.com, instantiates a CoinHive.User miner with the attacker's site key and a unique timestamp as the user identifier, and sends mined cryptocurrency shares to the attacker's account.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code variant loads a cryptomining script from coin-hive.com and starts mining in the user's browser without disclosure or consent, associating mining activity with a unique timestamp for tracking.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A maintenance page should not include or execute cryptomining scripts or load external resources unrelated to its stated function.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Opt-in cryptomining for fundraising or as an alternative to ads, but only with explicit user consent and clear communication.
key_indicators: Instantiation of CoinHive.User with a hardcoded site key and dynamic user identifier
No user notification or opt-in mechanism

attack_chain.action: User installs or deploys the maintainancewebsite npm package to serve a maintenance page.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious HTML/JS is served to site visitors.

attack_chain.action: When a visitor accesses the maintenance page, the browser loads the page containing the embedded cryptomining script.

The cryptomining script runs in the visitor's browser, consuming CPU resources and communicating with the coinhive.com or coin-hive.com service, crediting mined cryptocurrency to the attacker's account.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives mined cryptocurrency; user experiences degraded browser performance.

behavioral_signatures: HTML or JavaScript files in web packages that load coinhive.com or coin-hive.com cryptomining scripts
Instantiation of CoinHive.Anonymous or CoinHive.User objects in client-side code
Unexpected network requests to known cryptomining domains from maintenance or static pages
Significant browser CPU usage when visiting maintenance or static web pages
file_indicators: index.html or similar files containing <script src="https://coinhive.com/lib/coinhive.min.js"> or <script src="https://coin-hive.com/lib/coinhive.min.js">
References to CoinHive.Anonymous or CoinHive.User in HTML or JavaScript files
Unexplained or undocumented script tags in maintenance or static web page templates
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP(S) requests to coinhive.com or coin-hive.com
WebSocket or HTTP(S) connections to cryptomining service endpoints initiated by maintenance pages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan all HTML and JavaScript files in npm packages for script tags referencing known cryptomining domains such as coinhive.com or coin-hive.com. Flag any instantiation of CoinHive.Anonymous or CoinHive.User objects in client-side code. Monitor runtime network traffic from deployed web applications for connections to cryptomining services. Alert on unexpected spikes in browser CPU usage when visiting maintenance or static pages. Compare the contents of the published npm package with the public source repository to detect undocumented or removed malicious code.
